sources.title: Exact NVIDIA Super v1 model card
sources.evidence: Identifies NVIDIA’s Llama 3.3 70B Instruct derivative, released March 18, 2025, dense decoder-only Transformer with NAS-modified blocks, 131072-token text input/output, reasoning on/off and explicit tool-calling training. It names the NVIDIA and Llama 3.3 licenses.

sources.title: Pinned Super v1 configuration
sources.evidence: Specifies nemotron-nas / DeciLMForCausalLM, BF16, hidden width 8192, vocabulary 128256, untied embeddings, 80 block slots and 131072 maximum positions. There are 49 ordinary attention blocks, 31 skipped attention blocks and 80 dense FFNs with six intermediate widths; no expert routing or quantization.

sources.title: Official custom architecture implementation
sources.evidence: Defines learned embedding/head matrices, attention projections, dense gated FFNs and RMSNorms. Intermediate FFN width is ceil256(int(2*ffn_mult*hidden_size/3)). Skipped attention omits its input norm. RoPE inv_freq is a nonpersistent buffer, not a learned parameter.

sources.title: Official complete checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: The index maps 568 tensors to 21 shards and records 99734290432 data bytes. Every indexed tensor was reconciled with a header tensor and its configuration/code-derived shape.

sources.title: Official safetensors headers (first of 21 shards)
sources.evidence: Bounded bytes 0–65535 requests to all 21 shards returned HTTP 206. All 568 tensors are BF16 learned weights; shape products total 49867145216. Byte offsets are contiguous within each shard and each tensor uses two bytes per element. No scales, packed weights or buffers were counted.

sources.title: Official Hugging Face checkpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 API read reconfirms revision 387156d8d6868c19f3472fa607aa9bfc4f662333 and 49,867,145,216 BF16 parameters. This matches the previously verified header census and the independently recomputed configuration/code formula; no weight shards were fetched in this re-audit.

sources.title: Llama-Nemotron technical report, September 2025 revision
sources.evidence: Freshly rechecked full September 2025 report: names and links exact Super v1, reports nominal 49B, and describes NAS attention removal and FFN compression before post-training. Section 2 reserves FFN Fusion for Ultra. No separate Super active-parameter count is defined; the original Llama 3.3 70B count cannot transfer through this structural compression.

sources.title: Contemporaneous NVIDIA launch announcement
sources.evidence: The March 18, 2025 NVIDIA announcement identifies Super as 49B distilled from Llama 3.3 70B and distinguishes it from the then-forthcoming Ultra. This corroborates the exact card’s explicit release date.

sources.title: NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement
sources.evidence: The actual agreement linked as governing terms by the exact model card. The currently served page is marked last modified October 24, 2025; this is not used as a model release date.

sources.title: Llama 3.3 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: The exact underlying Llama agreement additionally linked by the model card. The agreement addresses Llama materials and derivative works.

sources.title: NVIDIA Llama Nemotron training and launch article
sources.evidence: The article states it was originally published March 18, 2025 and identifies Super as the 49B Llama 3.3 70B derivative. It describes the reasoning toggle and training process. Current text includes later updates, so the contemporaneous forum and explicit card date are the release-day evidence.

sources.title: Vultr original Nemotron Super v1.5 inference benchmark
sources.evidence: March 11, 2026 guide identifies nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-FP8 and separately lists Total Parameters 49B and Active Parameters 49B per token. It publishes its own HGX B200 FP8/BF16 benchmark results and reproducible serving configuration. This establishes Vultr's nominal benchmark convention, not a NVIDIA active-count disclosure or exact per-token tensor census. Transfer to v1 depends on the separately checked NVIDIA lineage and unchanged learned architecture.

sources.title: NVIDIA Super v1.5 card: explicit v1 upgrade and post-training
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies v1.5 as a significantly upgraded version of Super v1 and describes SFT, RPO, RLVR and iterative DPO, followed by merging RL/DPO checkpoints. It does not separately publish an active count. The named version relationship, supplemented by matching official learned-architecture configuration and implementation, supports a qualified nominal-count lineage inference rather than family resemblance alone.

sources.title: Pinned NVIDIA Super v1.5 configuration compared with v1
sources.evidence: Fresh direct comparison with pinned v1 config finds only _name_or_path and rope_scaling.factor (8 to 16) differ. All learned-architecture settings, all 80 block configurations, vocabulary, embedding tying, widths and attention heads are identical. RoPE frequency buffers are nonpersistent in the identical implementation, so this scaling change neither adds learned weights nor changes the parameter participation topology.

sources.title: Pinned NVIDIA Super v1.5 implementation identical to v1
sources.evidence: Freshly downloaded 78,580-byte modeling_decilm.py is byte-identical to pinned v1 implementation s3. Combined with matching learned-architecture config this verifies the same parameterized modules and forward structure; RoPE inv_freq is registered with persistent=False. No weight shards were fetched.

sources.title: NVIDIA Super v1.5 FP8 card and named lineage
sources.evidence: The exact checkpoint benchmarked by Vultr is explicitly identified as Super v1.5 FP8 and an upgrade of Super v1, with the same SFT/RL/DPO post-training description. Release links identify the BF16 v1.5 checkpoint and usage selects modelopt quantization. It does not provide an independent active-count disclosure.

sources.title: Pinned NVIDIA Super v1.5 FP8 configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh direct comparison with pinned BF16 v1.5 config finds only the descriptive _name_or_path differs. Every learned-architecture field and block configuration is identical. This closes the FP8-to-BF16 identity check needed for using Vultr's nominal convention; numerical precision is not treated as a change in nominal learned model size.

name.note: Display spelling matches the exact v1 checkpoint; it is separate from v1.5 and later Nemotron Super generations.

developer.note: NVIDIA is the model developer; Meta supplies the underlying Llama 3.3 model.

family.note: The official card places this exact model in the Llama Nemotron collection.

release_date.note: Explicit exact-model release date in the card agrees with the contemporaneous NVIDIA announcement. This is not the technical report’s later publication date.

open_weights.note: Full official BF16 checkpoint is downloadable; all 21 shard headers were accessed.

license.value: NVIDIA Open Model License + Llama 3.3 Community License
license.note: The model card names NVIDIA Open Model License as governing terms and additionally links Llama 3.3 Community License. The combined value records both named agreements.

parameters_b.note: Exact complete BF16 checkpoint: 49,867,145,216 learned parameters in 568 tensors, retained at full precision. Fresh October 27 API metadata and independent configuration/code arithmetic reconfirm the prior header census without downloading shards. Let D=8192 and V=128256. Count = 2*V*D + D + 49*(2*D*D + 2*D*1024 + D) + sum(3*D*I + D) over 80 FFNs. I frequencies: 28672×49, 14336×6, 17920×1, 7168×10, 5632×8, 2816×6. Includes embeddings and norms; excludes nonpersistent RoPE buffers. NVIDIA's 49B model label is nominal.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 49B active, inferred from Vultr's explicitly published v1.5 FP8/BF16 benchmark convention through NVIDIA's named v1-to-v1.5 upgrade and post-training lineage. Fresh official config comparisons show identical learned architectures for v1, v1.5 and v1.5 FP8; BF16 v1/v1.5 implementation is byte-identical. The v1.5 RoPE scale changes from 8 to 16 but acts on nonpersistent frequency buffers, not learned weights. This is not a separate NVIDIA v1 active-count disclosure and does not establish exact per-token tensor participation. Preserve Vultr's nominal 49B precision separately from the 49.867145216B checkpoint total; do not substitute the pruned Llama 3.3 70B predecessor's active count.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer customized with Puzzle NAS. Of 80 block slots, 49 retain GQA (64 query heads, 8 KV heads), 31 omit attention, and all 80 retain dense SwiGLU FFNs with variable widths. No experts or router. The report specifically applies FFN Fusion to Ultra; it is not attributed to this Super v1 checkpoint.

context_window.note: Exact model card and configuration agree on 131072 tokens; rounded 128K labels do not change the value. Example serving commands using 32768 are deployment settings.

modalities.note: Exact card explicitly specifies text input and output; this is a language-only causal model.

reasoning.note: The model is trained for reasoning and supports detailed thinking on/off in the system prompt, with think-tag output. This is documented model behavior rather than a generic prompting inference.

tool_call.note: Exact card documents tool-calling SFT and BFCL V2 Live evaluation with a tool-call format; this establishes model capability beyond inherited tokenizer syntax.

description.value: NVIDIA’s dense Llama 3.3 70B Instruct derivative, compressed through neural architecture search and post-trained for reasoning, chat and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces the generic claim about specialized agents with the documented base, NAS compression and post-training tasks.

patch.license: NVIDIA Open Model License + Llama 3.3 Community License
patch.description: NVIDIA’s dense Llama 3.3 70B Instruct derivative, compressed through neural architecture search and post-trained for reasoning, chat and tool calling.
patch.notes: Exact checkpoint total is 49.867145216B. Active 49B is a nominal inference from Vultr's v1.5 benchmark convention: NVIDIA identifies v1.5 as a v1 upgrade, and official configurations and implementation preserve the learned architecture. It is not a separate NVIDIA v1 active-count disclosure or exact per-token tensor census. Super v1 has 49 attention blocks and 80 variable-width FFNs; the technical report's FFN Fusion applies to Ultra.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains the exact 49.867145216B total, reconfirmed from official metadata and code/config arithmetic. Adds nominal 49B active as an explicit lineage inference from Vultr's original v1.5 FP8/BF16 benchmark convention: NVIDIA names v1.5 as the v1 upgrade and documents post-training; direct configuration and implementation comparisons verify unchanged learned architecture. NVIDIA's exact v1 card and original technical report still do not independently disclose active parameters, and no exact per-token census is claimed. All twelve other audited field assessments are unchanged.
